description.narrative:
This project strengthens inclusive, community based protection structures in conflict and climate affected district by combining Group Cash Transfers (GCT) with targeted capacity building. Through the GCT approach, community groups receive flexible funding to identify protection risks and implement their own context specific solutions, fostering local ownership and sustainability.
Somalia’s protracted crisis continues to expose civilians to intersecting layers of conflict, displacement, and socioeconomic hardship. Communities face persistent insecurity while simultaneously recovering from drought, adapting to rapid urbanization, and coping with rising living costs all of which heighten predictable and preventable protection risks. Women and girls are routinely exposed to harassment and violence during daily livelihood activities, while men and adolescent boys face movement restrictions, coercion, and extortion. Children are increasingly pushed into hazardous labour or early marriage as families struggle to meet basic needs. In Beledweyne,a city divided by the Shabelle River in Hiraan region, climate related shocks further intensify vulnerability. The area experiencesrecurrent flooding and drought, with recent floods submerging extensive farmland and severely undermining local agriculture and household resilience. Restricted freedom of movement due to conflict dynamics and the presence of non state armed actors further compounds protection concerns. Despite these widespread risks, protection remains insufficiently recognized as a lifesaving component of humanitarian response. Services are limited or absent in many locations, referral pathways remain fragmented, and existing community structures though active are overburdened with responsibilities that far exceed their capacity and mandate. This context underscoresthe urgent need for strengthened, community driven protection systems that can effectively identify, mitigate, and respond to evolving threats.
Oxfam and SSWC will support groups with outreach, transparent selection, and grant agreements that define roles, responsibilities, and risk mitigation measures. The project provides structured training on safeguarding, gender, protection, inclusion, and financial accountability, complemented bycoaching, peer learning, and cocreation spaces that reinforce governance and collectivedecision making. Participatory protection research will further help communities identify priority concerns, inform GCT interventions, guide adaptive programming, andstrengthen evidence-based advocacy.
Specific objective 1: Strengthen the capacity, governance, and accountability of community groups by providing Group Cash Transfers (GCT), participatory capacity strengthening, and ongoing coaching, and by supportinggroups to design and implement protection-outcome-oriented mini-projects that identify, mitigate, and respond to locally identified protection risks. Key Activities 1. Conduct community outreach and sensitization on the GCT approach, project goals, eligibility criteria. 2. Support groups to develop protection outcome-oriented mini-projects and group cash transfer (GCT)proposals that address locally identified protection risks, and formalize grant agreements outlining roles and responsibilities, risk mitigation measures, and reporting requirements. 3. Deliver structured capacity-building sessions on community-based protection (CBP), gender and inclusion, financial management, and accountability. Support groups to identify priority thematic areas where additional capacity strengthening is needed and tailor support accordingly.
4. Disburse Group Cash Transfers (GCT) selected community groups in tranches linked to milestones and accountability measures and accompany them in the implementation phase. 5. Provide ongoingcoaching, peer learning forums, and mentorship to strengthen decision making, internal governance, and conflict sensitive resource use.
Specific objective 2: To generate ethical, inclusive, and community driven protection evidencethrough participatory thematic research led by trained community members, informing localized protection planning, comparative risk analysis, and advocacy.
Key activities 1. Engage communities in identifying priority protection themes through participatory workshops and protection risk mapping. 2. Co develop research questions and research design with community groups to ensure relevance, feasibility, and ethical compliance. 3. Select and train community members as enumerators in ethical data collection, qualitative and quantitative data tools etc. 4. Conduct community-led data collection using trained enumerators and inclusive methodologies. 5. Facilitate community validation workshops to review findings and ensure accuracy and contextual relevance. 6. Analyze and synthesize protection evidence for use in comparative risk analysis, adaptation of GCT actions, and advocacy.

participating-org.narrative: It is a Somali women non-governmental humanitarian organization at a national level founded in 1992 at Mogadishu - the capital city, by a group of Somali women intellectuals from cross-section of the community. The Save Somali Women and Children (SSWC) contributeto the creation of a safe and sustainable situation by supporting women to overcome marginalization, violence and poverty in their communities. It operates as a non-profit making organization that has the right to network with a variety of organizations that share similar values and vision. In Somalia women face a range of complex challenges that require multiple solutions. We work in the belief that women through their own efforts and in collaboration with local, national and international allies are central to transforming their own lives and the lives of their communities and population of which they are part. SSWC is women-led and women-centered organization (so its programs reflect the needs of those served) that have well functioning management, finance and programmatic structures and systems.
